No unconditional leaderboard construction is submitted.

The unique dimension-1649 frontier inside the audited architecture would require an explicit binary inner code `B=[16384,17,8188]_2`. Given such a `B`, fix `F=GF(2^17)` by the lexicographically first irreducible monic degree-17 polynomial, fix an `F_2`-linear isomorphism `F→B`, and concatenate the ordinary Reed–Solomon code `[65536,97,65440]_F` evaluated on the first 65536 field elements in coefficient-vector order. This would deterministically give

`[16384·65536,17·97,≥8188·65440]_2 = [1073741824,1649,≥535822720]_2`.

The essential inner code is neither constructed nor proved to exist, so this is only a conditional gateway. A `[16384,16,8188]_2` inner code would similarly give dimension 1552 over `GF(2^16)`, and `[16384,18,8184]_2` would give dimension 1170; neither constituent is presently supplied.

Using the published exact value `N_2(9,64)=133`, one obtains `N_2(16,8189)≥8189+4095+2048+1024+512+256+128+133=16385`. Hence no `[16384,16,≥8189]_2` exists. Thus `m≤15`. Combined with the finite sieve, every ordinary product-certified RS concatenation in the audited range whose inner code contains all-one has final dimension at most 1040.

proof_markdown:
## Theorem and scope

Let `D=535822336`. Consider a binary inner code `B=[2^s,m,d]_2`, an ordinary Reed–Solomon outer code `[L,K,L−K+1]` over `GF(2^m)`, and any fixed injective binary-linear identification of an outer symbol with an inner word. Assume `1≤m≤30`, `L≤min(2^m,2^(30−s))`, and pad unused final coordinates by zero. I prove that the resulting code cannot have both product-certified distance at least `D` and dimension greater than 1649. If `B` contains the all-one word, its dimension cannot exceed 1040.

This is a scoped obstruction, not a global upper bound on binary codes.

## 1. Concatenation parameters

The outer evaluation map and inner encoder are linear and injective, so the binary dimension is exactly `mK`. A nonzero outer word has at least `L−K+1` nonzero symbols, each encoded to a word of weight at least `d`. Therefore

`d_min≥d(L−K+1)`.

Let `L_max=min(2^m,2^(30−s))`. Replacing `L` by `L_max` only makes the required distance easier to satisfy. Partition off `mK≤1040`. Otherwise

`K≥K_0=floor(1040/m)+1`

and necessarily

`d≥delta(s,m)=ceil(D/(L_max−K_0+1))`.

The binary Griesmer bound then requires

`g_m(delta):=Σ_{i=0}^{m−1}ceil(delta/2^i)≤2^s`. `(1)`

## 2. Exact finite sieve

If `m<8`, then `mK≤m2^m≤896`. If `m≥8` and `m+s≤29`, then `L_max=2^m` and `delta>D/2^m`, whence

`g_m(delta)/2^s > (2−2^(1−m))D/2^(m+s) ≥ (255/128)(511/512)>1`.

Thus only `m+s≥30` remains. Direct integer evaluation of `(1)` gives positive minimum gaps for `s=5,…,12`:

`19,17,15,13,11,9,6,1`,

and for `s=16,…,23`:

`36,315,1700,7832,33916,144802,632944,3011882`.

For `s≤4`, `m+s≥30` contradicts `m≤2^s`. At `s=24`, an improvement forces `K≥35`; since `L_max≤64`, even `d=2^24` gives product at most `30·2^24<D`. For `s≥25`, `mK≤30·2^(30−s)≤960`.

The only raw survivors are therefore:

- `s=13`, `17≤m≤24`, all requiring `d≥4090`;
- `s=14`, `16≤m≤30`, with the exact thresholds listed in the parameter ledger;
- `s=15`, `17≤m≤30`, with the exact thresholds listed there.

## 3. Degree-three spherical bound

Map a binary length-`N` code to normalized sign vectors. Distance at least `d_0` gives maximum inner product `sigma=(N−2d_0)/N=a/N`. For

`0≤sigma≤(sqrt(N+3)−1)/(N+2)=1/(sqrt(N+3)+1)`,

the degree-three Levenshtein theorem gives

`|C|≤L_3(N,d_0):=(N−a)(2N+(N+1)a)/(N−a^2)`. `(2)`

Every use below has `N≥8192` and `a≤32`; hence `a/N≤1/256<1/183<1/(sqrt(N+3)+1)`. Exact substitution and flooring gives:

| `N` | `d_0` | `a` | `floor L_3` | consequence |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---|
|8192|4090|12|116581|less than `2^17`; all `s=13` survivors fail|
|16384|8183|18|333941|less than `2^19`; rank 19 fails|
|16384|8176|32|593066|less than `2^20`; ranks at least 20 fail by taking a 20-dimensional subcode|
|16385|8190|5|114840|less than `2^17`|
|16385|8186|13|248152|less than `2^18`|
|32769|16384|1|98308|less than `2^17`|
|32769|16382|5|229528|less than `2^18`|
|32768|16379|10|394309|less than `2^19`|
|32768|16378|12|460620|less than `2^20`|
|32768|16369|30|1077233|less than `2^21`; ranks at least 21 fail by subcoding|

Appending an overall parity coordinate to a binary code of minimum distance at least an odd integer `t` produces distance at least `t+1`. Thus rows four and five show respectively that a length-16384 rank-17 code has `d≤8188` and a rank-18 code has `d≤8184`. The last five rows eliminate every `s=15` survivor. Only `s=14` and ranks 16–18 remain.

## 4. Residual-table improvement

Let `N_2(k,d)` denote the least length of a binary linear code of dimension `k` and distance at least `d`. Choose an actual minimum word `c` of weight `w≥d` and restrict the code to the complement of `supp(c)`. The restriction kernel is exactly `span{c}`: any other kernel word `x` would make both `x` and `x+c` nonzero, although their weights sum to `w`, contradicting minimality of `w`.

For a lift `x` whose outside-support weight is `b`,

`wt(x)+wt(x+c)=w+2b≥2w`,

so `b≥ceil(w/2)`. Monotonicity therefore yields the residual recurrence

`N_2(k,d)≥d+N_2(k−1,ceil(d/2))`. `(3)`

Dodunekov–Guritman–Simonis proved the exact value `N_2(9,64)=133`. Iterating `(3)` gives

`N_2(16,8189) ≥ 8189+4095+2048+1024+512+256+128+N_2(9,64)`

`=16252+133=16385`.

Consequently no `[16384,16,≥8189]_2` exists, and rank 16 also has `d≤8188`.

## 5. Exact rounding and the ceiling

For inner exponent `r` with `11≤r≤15`, put

`h=2^(r−10)`, `N=2^(30−r)`, `c=2^(31−2r)`.

Then `N=c·512h` and `D=511hN`. If `d=511h+j` with `1≤j<h`, then

`d(N−cj)−D=cj(h−j)>0`,

whereas `cj(h−j)≤ch^2/4=512<d`; hence `d(N−cj−1)<D`. Therefore

`ceil(D/d)=N−cj`. `(4)`

At `r=14`, `(h,c,N)=(16,8,65536)`. For ranks 16 and 17, `d≤8188=8176+12`, so `(4)` gives `ceil(D/d)≥65440`, hence `K≤97`. Their final dimensions are at most 1552 and 1649. For rank 18, `d≤8184=8176+8`, so `ceil(D/d)≥65472`, `K≤65`, and `18K≤1170`. This proves the dimension-1649 ceiling.

## 6. All-one inner obstruction

Suppose `1∈B`, where `B` has length `N`, dimension `m`, and minimum distance `d≤N/2`; put `a=N−2d` and assume `a^2<N`. Choose one representative from each coset of `B/<1>`. For two distinct representatives, their difference is neither zero nor one, so its weight lies in `[d,N−d]`. The corresponding normalized sign vectors therefore have absolute inner products at most `a/N`.

For their `M=2^(m−1)` Gram matrix `G`, rank at most `N` and eigenvalue Cauchy–Schwarz give

`M^2=(tr G)^2≤N tr(G^2)≤N[M+M(M−1)a^2/N^2]`.

Thus

`M≤(N^2−a^2)/(N−a^2)`. `(5)`

After the general eliminations, any architecture exceeding 1040 would have `N=16384`, `m≥16`, and `d≥8184`, so `a≤16`. Equation `(5)` gives

`2^(m−1)≤(16384^2−16^2)/(16384−16^2)=1048575/63=16644+1/21<32768`,

a contradiction. Hence every all-one-inner architecture in scope has dimension at most 1040.

## 7. Exact unresolved frontier

Equality in the general ceiling can only use `s=14`, `m=17`, `d=8188`, `L=65536`, and `K=97`. Thus it requires a non-antipodal `[16384,17,8188]_2` inner code. Residualization forces `[8196,16,4094]` and then `[4102,15,≥2047]`; a proof `N_2(10,64)≥136` would exclude it. The historical GUAVA data instead leave `63≤d_2(135,10)≤64`, so no exclusion or construction is inferred. The dimension-1649 route remains conditional.

proof_steps.proof: Injectivity of the inner symbol map and the outer evaluation map gives dimension `mK`. Every nonzero outer word has at least `L−K+1` nonzero symbols, proving product distance `d(L−K+1)`; zero padding preserves both quantities.
proof_steps.statement: The audited concatenation has exact binary dimension `mK` and product-certified distance at least `d(L−K+1)`.

proof_steps.proof: Use `K_0=floor(1040/m)+1`, the most favorable length `L_max`, and the necessary Griesmer inequality at `delta=ceil(D/(L_max−K_0+1))`. The field-limited region is eliminated analytically; exact integer evaluation leaves only the stated `s=13,14,15` rows.
proof_steps.statement: Any scoped concatenation with dimension above 1040 must occur in the explicitly listed finite survivor set.

proof_steps.proof: The normalized sign embedding converts each required binary distance to a maximum spherical inner product. All hypotheses of the degree-three bound hold, and the exact rational floors listed in the proof eliminate `s=13`, `s=15`, and ranks at least 19 for `s=14`; parity extension supplies the rank-17 and rank-18 endpoint ceilings.
proof_steps.statement: Only length-16384 inner ranks 16–18 survive, with rank-17 distance at most 8188 and rank-18 distance at most 8184.

proof_steps.proof: Restriction outside an actual minimum word has kernel exactly its span and distance at least half its weight, giving `N_2(k,d)≥d+N_2(k−1,ceil(d/2))`.
proof_steps.statement: The binary residual minimum-length recurrence holds.

proof_steps.proof: For `d=511h+j`, direct multiplication shows `d(N−cj)>D` but `d(N−cj−1)<D`, since the positive excess is at most 512 and is smaller than `d`.
The three remaining rank caps are respectively `16·97=1552`, `17·97=1649`, and `18·65=1170`; every discarded branch was already at most 1040 or impossible.
proof_steps.statement: Every code in the audited ordinary-RS architecture has binary dimension at most 1649.

proof_steps.proof: Quotient by complements, embed coset representatives as signs, and combine the absolute inner-product bound with Gram rank. At the only remaining block length this bounds the quotient size below `2^15`, contradicting inner rank at least 16.
proof_steps.statement: If the inner code contains all-one, the final scoped dimension is at most 1040.

proof_steps.proof: The only cap attaining 1649 is `m=17,K=97`; exact distance rounding forces `s=14,d=8188,L=65536`. No generator for the required inner code is known, and the residual endpoint remains unresolved.
proof_steps.statement: A `[16384,17,8188]_2` inner code would yield `[2^30,1649,≥535822720]_2` by deterministic RS concatenation.

research_direction: Exact finite-length rounding optimization for ordinary equal-block Reed–Solomon concatenations, strengthened by residual minimum-length tables and an all-one quotient bound.
theorem_statement: Let `B` be a binary linear `[2^s,m,d]_2` code with `1≤m≤30`, and concatenate it with an ordinary `[L,K,L−K+1]` Reed–Solomon code over `GF(2^m)`, where `L≤min(2^m,2^(30−s))`; zero-pad to length `2^30` and certify distance by `d(L−K+1)`. If the certified distance is at least `535822336`, then `mK≤1649`. If `B` contains the all-one word, then `mK≤1040`. Equality 1649 can occur only through an unresolved non-antipodal inner `[16384,17,8188]_2` and outer `[65536,97,65440]_(2^17)`; no existence claim is made.
title: Residual-table closure lowers the small-field ordinary-RS ceiling from 1808 to 1649
